title: fix(cli,plugin-security): os migrate organization-ownership --apply resolves the built-in positions and the everyone baseline
body:
Fixes #23397
Clause-②: no (the `authored-conversion` guard and the rewrite gate are unchanged; the catalog they read gains what a started kernel already serves, per `schema-migration-plugins.ts`'s "What a schema command needs from a plugin is its DECLARATIONS, and the kernel contract puts those in `init()`"; no export is added)

## What was wrong

`os migrate organization-ownership --apply` boots the deployment's served composition with every platform provider composed for its declarations only. The security plugin's `init()` runs; its `start()` and every hook do not. The plugin declared the six built-in positions in `start()`, and `everyone`'s baseline from a `kernel:ready` hook registered in `start()`. So the ceremony's catalog held neither, and every 17.x database's seeded `everyone` to `member_default` binding blocked the ceremony.

## What changed (route (a) of the card, inside `plugin-security`)

- `SecurityPlugin.init()` declares the six built-in positions, with `everyone` naming the deployment's baseline (the app's `isDefault` set composed with `member_default`), through the same `registerBuiltinPositions` / `declareEveryoneBaseline` seam as before. These are registry writes only. No database read or write is added.
- The baseline in `init()` is the **fail-closed reading**: the high-privilege check runs with no declared-capability context, because the stack's declarations are still arriving while plugins initialize. With no context a token is never excused, so this list is never wider than the one `kernel:ready` derives.
- `kernel:ready`'s `declareEveryone` is unchanged in what it computes. It runs the check against every declared capability, adds the accepted package defaults (a database read, which stays there), and replaces the `init()` declaration. The baseline filter is one private method that both call (`everyoneBaseline`), so there is no second derivation.
- The "the built-in positions … were NOT declared as position metadata" warning moved with the declaration into `init()`. It still fires when the engine exposes no registry. When no engine is registered, `init()` says nothing, because `start()` already reports that.
- No cli source changed: no new export, no host workaround, and nothing in `organization-ownership-apply.ts`, `organization-ownership-plan.ts` or `schema-migration-plugins.ts`.

## What a started kernel sees

Its catalog after boot is the same. Three things move:

1. The six positions and `everyone`'s baseline are in the engine registry from the plugin's `init()` instead of from `start()` and `kernel:ready`. Any reader between the two now sees the final names earlier.
2. If the `kernel:ready` derivation throws, `everyone` keeps the `init()` baseline. It used to name no set.
3. The no-registry warning prints from `init()`.

Unchanged: the cold boot's environment-held-name refusal skips the built-in names, as it did. A stored definition under a built-in name still shadows the declaration at read. objectql's `protocol-boot-hydration-scoped.test.ts` control already declares the built-in in Phase 1 and holds both.

## Measurement of the dispatch hypotheses (on `5656c5638`)

- **H1 (confirmed).** `registerBuiltinPositions` was in `start()`, and `declareEveryoneBaseline` was inside `declareEveryone`, which ran from a `kernel:ready` hook registered in `start()`. The apply boot composes the security plugin twice: once through `composeAuthGatedSecurity` (`composeForDeclarations`) and once in the served platform's auth family (`composeProviderForDeclarations`). The kernel keeps the later one, so the surviving instance is the provider posture, which withholds every hook including `kernel:ready`. Measured: the boot logs "Plugin superseded: 'com.objectstack.security' — the later registration REPLACED the earlier one". So only `init()` runs, and a `kernel:ready` hook registered from `init()` would not have reached the ceremony either.
- **H2 (confirmed).** `ql.registry` is reachable in `init()`: the plugin depends on `com.objectstack.engine.objectql`, and `init()` already reads that plugin's `manifest` service. No reader depends on the declaration happening in `start()`. The cold-boot check skips the built-in names, the item seam's built-in carve-out holds in either order, and the plugin-security, plugin-auth, rest, runtime and organizations suites listed below are green.
- **H3.** Both `authored-conversion` and the rewrite gate compare the binding rows against the `permissionSets` that the catalog's position definition names (`declaredPositionSets`, which feeds `convertPositionBindingRows`). The fate must be `declared`. `authored-conversion` additionally needs the position to exist. So both need the built-in position and the deployment baseline. The accepted-default half is a `sys_audience_binding_suggestion` read and stays at `kernel:ready`; the ceremony does not read it (Acceptance notes).
- **H4 (held).** No write is added on `os migrate plan`. The no-write pins stay green: `schema-migrate.host-composition.integration.test.ts` ("writes NOTHING while planning — no host seeder runs", "still writes NOTHING — the declaration-phase suppression is intact", the #13332 "THE FIX: the declaration boot lands none of them"), `schema-migration-plugins.declaration-boot-write-guard.test.ts` and `security-catalog-overlays.integration.test.ts`: 3 files, 40 tests passed.

## Proof

**The card's own case, the real command.** I ran `os migrate organization-ownership --apply --backup-taken --json` in-process against a database that this release's apply composition provisioned, plus the 17.x rows: the seeded `everyone` position, `member_default` and the binding between them, with no `org_member` binding.

| | before (old placement, dist rebuilt) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `single` | `authored-conversion` **blocked**: "Binding rows give position everyone the sets member_default, and the catalog holds no position of that name to carry them." | `authored-conversion` done, `rewrite` done, `mirror-deletion` deleted 3 |
| `OS_MULTI_ORG_ENABLED=true` (posture `isolated`) | `rewrite` **blocked**: "Binding rows give position everyone sets its catalog definition does not name (member_default); deleting them would lose a grant." | `rewrite` done, `mirror-deletion` deleted 3 |

After the fix, both runs stop at `column-drops` on `sys_metadata*`.`organization_id` ("not proposed for dropping"). That is the inventory's `column-drop` rows, out of bounds here.

**The pins:**

- `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.served-catalog.integration.test.ts`. It runs the apply command's boot flag for flag, with core's catalog reader, against the 17.x rows plus a control binding to `zz_undeclared`. It checks that the six built-ins resolve and `everyone` names `member_default`. Under `single`, `authored-conversion` blocks on the control alone. Walled, the rewrite gate blocks on the control alone. **A real conversion still blocks** when a binding names a position that is absent.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/builtin-positions.declaration-phase.test.ts`. It runs `init()` alone over a real engine registry. The six resolve, owned by the plugin. `everyone` names the app default and then `member_default`. The fail-closed reading leaves out a set whose token only a declaration excuses, and says nothing. The warning fires on an engine with no registry, and stays silent when no engine is registered.

**Negative control (one-shot, at `7f3b67b69`).** I restored `security-plugin.ts` from the base (on-disk hash `b042c660f9` equals the base blob) and rebuilt plugin-security. `ablation-dist-preflight --absent` showed the init call gone from all 6 built files. Then:

- the plugin pin goes red, 4 failed and 1 passed (the no-engine case);
- the cli pin goes red, 3 of 3 failed;
- the card's two messages above reproduce.

Restored with `git checkout HEAD`: hash `7a64f14215` equals the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. I rebuilt, and the preflight found the marker in 2 built files. Both pins are green again.

## The grant goldens moved by one recorded step

Four plugin-security goldens record a harness that runs `init()` and `start()` but fires no `kernel:ready`:

- `grant-permission-set-name.equivalence.test.ts`
- `grant-permission-set-name-backfill.test.ts`
- `grant-readers-by-name.golden.test.ts`
- `resolve-authz-grant-set-by-name.golden.test.ts`

In that harness `everyone` used to name nothing. It now names the baseline, so every principal holding `everyone` gains `member_default`, and nothing else moves. That is what a started kernel's `kernel:ready` derivation has always given: `builtin-positions.boot.test.ts`'s grant golden, which fires the hooks, already carries `member_default` for every principal and is unchanged. Each golden's note records the move. The backfill's "an unnamed grant confers nothing" check now asserts exactly `['member_default']` (what `everyone` names) instead of `[]`.

## Verification (final HEAD `1ebf9c5d7`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run`: 186 files, 3781 passed, 45 skipped. `typecheck`: exit 0.
- `@objectstack/cli` unit tier, in three shards: 96 + 96 + 95 files. Two `published-subpath-*` pins first reported PREREQUISITE NOT MET because the cli was not built; after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build` they pass, 29 tests. cli `typecheck`: exit 0.
- cli integration, the files named above: the new pin (3), plus the H4 set (40).
- Consumers that boot the plugin without `kernel:ready`: plugin-auth 5 files / 41, rest 9 files / 120, runtime `share-links-enforcement-context` 28, organizations `create-explicit-organization-wall` 21. All green.
- `dispatch-gates --ran`: 68 derived, 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, every family exit 0. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` first answered PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3, dist of unrelated packages); re-run with the dist present, both exit 0.
- `pnpm lint` (full `eslint .`) at `1ebf9c5d7`: exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- **The accepted package defaults stay out of the ceremony's catalog.** That half of `everyone` is a database read and stays at `kernel:ready`. A binding to a set that only a deployment-level acceptance puts on `everyone` still blocks the ceremony. A 17.x database holds no such acceptance (rows resolved before the deployment-level decision are re-opened as pending), so the card's population is unaffected. This is measured by reading, not reproduced. Carrier: none.
- **Two objectql comments now describe the old timing.** `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` around line 2795 and line 4468 say the platform declares its built-ins "in its own `start()`". It now does so in `init()`, and `everyone` is re-declared at `kernel:ready`. The built-in carve-out they explain is still load-bearing for that re-declaration. Not edited here: outside the claimed file surface. Carrier: none.
- **The curated capabilities are still declared in `start()`.** No ceremony step resolves a capability from the catalog: `authored-conversion` reports `sys_capability` rows without a catalog read. So this card does not need them.
- **#23359** (the apply without the security plugin composed) is not changed by this PR. Without the plugin, nothing declares the built-ins either, so on a 17.x database the ceremony still stops at `authored-conversion` on `everyone`, with the "Declare the position (or remove the bindings)" remedy. That is the same cause and remedy shape #23359 names for the shipped sets. #23359 remains open.
